title: Streamline log ingestion schema and indexing for multi-tenant Loki/ELK
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: reduce query latency and storage cost for tenant logs by standardizing a small, versioned structured-log schema, implementing targeted index mappings for Elasticsearch, and harmonizing Loki label usage. Scope: ingestion pipeline changes (Logstash/Fluent Bit -> buffers -> Loki/ELK), schema registry for log producers, parsers for legacy plain-text services, retention/index lifecycle policy updates, and dashboards/alerts for correctness and cost. Out of scope: changes to log producers' business logic beyond adding a lightweight logging shim; we will not replace existing tracing instrumentation in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: All backend services emit well-formed JSON logs for the defined schema version v1.1 (fields: timestamp, level, service, env, tenant_id, request_id, trace_id, span_id, event, msg, meta)
Loki label set reduced to canonical 'service','env','tenant_id','level' for tail queries; high-cardinality fields moved to JSON payload to avoid label blowup
Elasticsearch index templates updated and applied with optimized mappings and disabled _all; expected 20-30% reduction in storage for the same dataset
End-to-end ingestion (Fluent Bit -> staging -> Loki/ELK) demonstrates no more than 100ms median added latency under steady-state test with 5000 eps
Dashboards show correct correlation across logs and traces using request_id/trace_id; two sample queries documented
Migration runbook and rollback steps created and reviewed by SRE and Product; no high-severity customer incidents in 72h canary window
tasks: Design compact structured-log v1.1 schema and publish Confluence spec
Implement Fluent Bit config changes for JSON parsing and routing to staging topics
Build a lightweight logging shim (Go/Python) for legacy services to emit schema-compliant lines
Create Elasticsearch index templates and ILM policies (hot-warm-cold) with cost targets
Update Loki promtail/ingest pipeline to normalize labels and drop high-cardinality keys
Instrument end-to-end perf test harness (k6 + local replay) and run baseline vs post-change
Add unit/integration tests and CI jobs to validate sample payloads against schema
Prepare dashboards and SLO checks in Grafana; add alert for unexpected label cardinality growth
decisions: Use a minimal canonical label set in Loki to avoid high-cardinality costs; keep additional attributes in JSON body
Adopt schema versioning with a simple registry in Confluence + JSON Schema files in repo instead of a heavy service
Route tenant-specific high-volume logs to a lower-retention 'hot-short' index to reduce cost for noisy tenants
Prefer Fluent Bit parsing (at the edge) over post-ingest processors to reduce downstream CPU load
tradeoffs: Keeping fewer Loki labels reduces queryability for arbitrary fields — tradeoff mitigated by adding JSON field extraction examples in dashboards
Implementing a shim for legacy services requires per-service changes; faster rollout vs forcing immediate upstream changes
Index template changes risk reindexing costs if applied incorrectly — we will use new index aliasing and phased migration to avoid full reindex
